past_medical_history: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Graves disease treated with radioiodine 2 years ago, now hypothyroid on levothyroxine)

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Normal cognition and language.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left ptosis — levator excursion 4mm. Complete fatigable ptosis left eye on sustained upgaze at 35 seconds. Right ptosis mild intermittent. Esotropia left eye at rest (left medial rectus/adductor weakness causing false impression of esotropia — actually left lateral rectus weakness). Vertical diplopia on upgaze. Pupils equal, reactive. Bilateral mild facial weakness — patient unable to close eyes tightly against resistance. No proptosis.
neurological_exam.motor: Shoulder abductors 4/5 bilaterally. Hip flexors 4+/5. Neck flexors 4-/5. Distal strength 5/5. Fatigability: neck flexion fails after 30 seconds sustained effort.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal. Mildly waddling after walking one block.
neurological_exam.additional: Nasal voice quality after sustained speech. Difficulty chewing — jaw fatigues after 2-3 minutes eating. NIF -61 cmH2O (normal). No respiratory distress.

patient.chief_complaint: Left eyelid drooping with double vision and jaw fatigue for 8 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: A 29-year-old woman with a history of Graves disease treated with radioiodine (now hypothyroid on levothyroxine) presented with 8 weeks of left eyelid drooping, double vision, and jaw fatigue. She first noticed her left eyelid drooping while studying late at night approximately 8 weeks ago. Initially she thought it was related to sleep deprivation from graduate school deadlines. However, the ptosis persisted during the day and worsened in the afternoon. She started experiencing double vision approximately 6 weeks ago — she described seeing two images side by side when looking to the right, and vertical separation of images when looking up. She noticed that her jaw became very fatigued when eating — by the third or fourth bite of a tough food she needed to rest her jaw for 30 seconds before continuing. Her speech became noticeably nasal after she had been speaking for more than a few minutes. She denied any difficulty swallowing liquids or solids but acknowledged food 'sometimes takes longer to chew.' She has had no headache, no limb numbness or tingling, no falls, no bowel or bladder symptoms. She initially saw a student health clinic who attributed the ptosis to allergic conjunctivitis and treated her with antihistamine eye drops without improvement. She subsequently saw an ophthalmologist who ruled out structural eyelid pathology and confirmed no proptosis — noting her prior Graves disease history, the ophthalmologist was concerned about reactivation of thyroid eye disease. However, thyroid function tests performed 2 weeks ago were normal (TSH 2.2). She was then referred to neurology. Her family history includes thyroid disease and she had a recent flare of anxiety attributed to her graduate school stress, for which she declined medication.

findings.result: Complete resolution of left ptosis and esotropia within 45 seconds of IV edrophonium 10mg
findings.significance: Positive pharmacological response — complete resolution of ptosis and esotropia
Normal motor and sensory conduction; normal baseline CMAP amplitudes

specialized_test.impression: Clearly abnormal RNS with 15–24% decremental responses across facial, proximal limb, and masseter muscles. Positive edrophonium (Tensilon) test with complete resolution of ptosis and esotropia. Findings are consistent with a disorder of neuromuscular transmission

labs.interpretation: Anti-AChR binding antibody markedly elevated at 8.7 nmol/L (reference <0.5 nmol/L). Anti-AChR blocking and modulating antibodies elevated. Anti-MuSK negative. Anti-titin negative. Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in a subset of patients with neuromuscular junction disorders; elevated results are associated with autoimmune neuromuscular junction disease
abnormal_values_summary: Anti-AChR binding 8.7 nmol/L (markedly elevated; ref <0.5 nmol/L)

findings.description: Thymic tissue with fatty involution appropriate for age 29. No discrete mass. No thymoma identified.

ct.impression: No anterior mediastinal mass identified. Thymic tissue with fatty involution appropriate for age. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear

output.impression: Severely abnormal SFEMG with markedly increased jitter (mean MCD 82 µs) and high blocking rate (85%). Findings are consistent with a disorder of neuromuscular transmission

findings.description: No anterior mediastinal mass on repeat contrast-enhanced CT. Residual thymic tissue only.

output.impression: No anterior mediastinal mass on contrast-enhanced CT chest. Residual thymic tissue only. No lymphadenopathy

abnormal_values_summary: Anti-TPO 62 IU/mL (elevated; ref <35); TRAb negative; Clinical Activity Score 0/7

output.proposed: Pyridostigmine 60mg q4-6h AND prednisone 15mg daily AND azathioprine 50mg titrating to 2-3mg/kg for MG in patient on levothyroxine
interactions: Prednisone + levothyroxine: corticosteroids may reduce levothyroxine absorption — separate dosing by 2 hours
contraindications: Mycophenolate contraindicated — woman of reproductive age (teratogenic)
warnings: Levothyroxine absorption can be reduced by corticosteroids — advise taking levothyroxine 30-60 minutes before meals and 2h before prednisone
Monitor CBC monthly for first 3 months on azathioprine
alternatives: Azathioprine preferred over mycophenolate in this reproductive-age patient

output.query: MGTX trial thymectomy nonthymomatous myasthenia gravis evidence

results.title: Randomized Trial of Thymectomy in Myasthenia Gravis (MGTX)
results.finding: Thymectomy + prednisone superior to prednisone alone at 3 years in patients aged 18-65 with generalized AChR-positive MG; lower time-weighted average QMG score, less alternate-day prednisone, fewer hospitalizations, higher complete stable remission rate

results.title: MGTX 5-year follow-up
results.finding: Benefit of thymectomy over prednisone alone persisted at 5 years; 67% reduction in prednisone requirement; thymectomy recommended for all patients 18-65 with generalized AChR-positive MG regardless of CT chest findings

output.summary: MGTX trial (NEJM 2016, 5-year follow-up Lancet Neurology 2022) provides Class I evidence that thymectomy + prednisone is superior to prednisone alone in AChR antibody-positive generalized neuromuscular junction disease aged 18–65. Benefit was demonstrated regardless of CT chest findings.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), AChR antibody-positive, without thymoma; concurrent post-Graves autoimmune thyroid disease (now hypothyroid on levothyroxine)

differential.key_features: Treated Graves disease can have residual orbitopathy; pattern here is fatigable, not restrictive; markedly positive AChR confirms MG.
Levothyroxine over-replacement could cause weakness but not fatigable ptosis with RNS decrement.
Young patient without malignancy; baseline CMAPs normal; AChR markedly positive.
Demographic possibility for childbearing-age woman; fatigable ptosis is incompatible.
Markedly elevated AChR antibodies establish organic pathology.

optimal_actions.action: Order serologies: anti-AChR (binding, blocking, modulating), anti-MuSK, anti-LRP4, and TSH/free-T4 for thyroid autoimmunity
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AChR antibody positive; TSH evaluates for comorbid thyroid disease

optimal_actions.action: Order repetitive nerve stimulation (RNS) at 2-3 Hz across proximal and facial muscles
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Decrement >10% in symptomatic muscles supports postsynaptic NMJ disorder
Increased jitter and blocking on extensor digitorum communis or orbicularis oculi confirms NMJ transmission failure

optimal_actions.action: Order CT chest with contrast for thymoma screening
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No thymoma; thymic involution appropriate for age

optimal_actions.action: Review MGFA classification and current treatment guidance (pyridostigmine, prednisone, steroid-sparing, IVIG/PLEX, thymectomy)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MGFA classification stages disease severity; thymectomy benefits AChR+ generalized MG (MGTX); IVIG/PLEX for crisis

tool_parameters.query: myasthenia gravis MGFA classification treatment thymectomy

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions for MG-exacerbating agents (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, telithromycin, IV magnesium, neuromuscular blockers, procainamide)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Flag aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, IV magnesium, telithromycin, NMBs as contraindicated or use-with-caution in MG

optimal_actions.action: Bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) — repeat q4h in crisis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline FVC/NIF to assess crisis risk in patients with bulbar or limb involvement

optimal_actions.action: Bedside ice-pack test for ptosis (cheap, ~80% sensitive for ocular MG)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Improvement of ptosis after 2 minutes of cooling supports MG

useless_tools.rationale: MG is a peripheral neuromuscular junction disorder; EEG has no diagnostic role.
No CSF role in MG; LP risks complications without diagnostic yield.
Advanced imaging (PET/MR spectroscopy/perfusion) is not indicated for MG diagnosis or staging; CT chest covers thymoma screening.
Brain MRI is non-contributory in typical MG; reserve for cases where an alternative CNS cause (brainstem lesion, demyelination) is genuinely in the differential.
Echocardiography is not indicated for MG unless a comorbid cardiac question exists.
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated for MG unless arrhythmia or autonomic disease is independently suspected.

sequence_constraints.reason: Order AChR/MuSK/LRP4 serologies first; reserve single-fiber EMG for seronegative or RNS-non-diagnostic cases (resource stewardship).

critical_actions: CT chest — required in all confirmed MG (here negative for thymoma)
Single-fiber EMG given diagnostic clarity already achieved by serology + RNS
Coordinate steroid plan with endocrinology — thyroid status will shift with treatment
Counsel on pregnancy planning — MG can fluctuate during gestation, ensure safe medication regimen
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT prescribe aminoglycoside antibiotics (gentamicin, tobramycin, amikacin) — risk of precipitating myasthenic crisis
Do NOT prescribe fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin) — FDA black-box warning for MG exacerbation
Do NOT prescribe telithromycin — contraindicated in MG
Do NOT administer IV magnesium for MG patients (e.g., for hypomagnesaemia, eclampsia prophylaxis) without alternative — blocks NMJ transmission
Do NOT use non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockers without anaesthesia/MG-aware dosing protocols
Do NOT initiate high-dose corticosteroids as sole outpatient therapy without hospitalization or pyridostigmine bridge — risk of paradoxical worsening at days 5-10
Do NOT attribute fluctuating fatigable weakness to a functional disorder before completing serology + RNS + single-fiber EMG workup
key_reasoning_points: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with diurnal pattern (worse evening) is the clinical hallmark of MG — fixed weakness suggests an alternative diagnosis.
Ocular involvement (ptosis, diplopia) is asymmetric and fatigable in MG; thyroid eye disease causes restrictive (not fatigable) ophthalmoplegia.
Single-fiber EMG (sensitivity >95%) is the most sensitive electrodiagnostic test — order when RNS is non-diagnostic or serology is negative.
All confirmed MG cases require CT chest for thymoma — present in roughly 10-15% of generalized MG; thymectomy (MGTX trial) improves long-term outcomes in non-thymoma AChR+ MG as well.
Aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, telithromycin, IV magnesium, and neuromuscular blockers can precipitate myasthenic crisis and must be screened against any new prescription.
Post-Graves autoimmune background increases MG risk (polyautoimmunity); recognize this co-occurrence rather than re-attribute MG symptoms to thyroid disease.
Childbearing-age woman: address contraception and pre-pregnancy MG management early.

red_herrings.data_point: Treated Graves disease, now hypothyroid on levothyroxine
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute ocular symptoms to residual Graves orbitopathy.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Graves orbitopathy is restrictive and gives proptosis/lid retraction; this is fatigable and AChR-antibody positive — independent MG.
